learning_outcomes.text: Know the different types of computers, along with their characteristics and capabilities, that can be used as hardware support in the design and development of a computer system.
Be able to select and evaluate the most appropriate type of computer to provide a service ensuring the required quality characteristics.
Evaluate computer organization alternatives to improve their performance.
Understand the operation of the mechanisms provided by the architecture to support multitasking operating systems.
Know examples of the architecture and organization of real systems.

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as NTeo x 0.5 + NPrac x 0.4 + TGrup x 0.1, where NTeo is the theoretical part, NPrac the practical part, and TGrup the group work. A minimum score of 40% is required in both NTeo and NPrac to pass; otherwise, the final grade will be the lesser of 4.5 points and the calculated grade. For the extraordinary call, if the practical qualification (NPrac) is 50% or higher and the ordinary call resulted in a fail, the NPrac score can be retained. The evaluation for students with differentiated assessment is Nota = NTeo x 0.5 + NPrac x 0.5, with the same minimum score requirements. Fraudulent activity in any assessable test will result in a 0-Fail grade.
